title: Review of FCH chemoton (SIBE): on seed 5 no catalyst-carrying vesicle forms (the catalyst sits on an open strip), the starvation fork works; Weak
summary: After the claim's sheets and starve_fork.png, I re-ran world.py and world_starve.py on seed 5 (200 frames, t=600, 192^2). From the noisy bath ~10 bodies form by t=24 and grow into bilayer strands and two small closed rings by t=51-81. The catalyst survives on only one body, an open bilayer strip (a rod with K along it, t=81-600, with a dark precursor-depletion halo); the closed rings carry no K and live on amphiphile from the bath, as on the author's seed 1. labkit finds no membrane-like layer on this seed (u aggregate rim/core 0.83, 6/36 individuals; K rim/core 0.54, 0/36). With the feed cut at t=300 the strip breaks into micelles and ends as one dot, and the other strands shrink to dots: total amphiphile 1984 (fed) vs 323 (starved) at t=600, K 1392 vs 215 (totals.txt).

observations.I: rerun_/sheet.png: the K-bearing strip and two rings persist t~81-600 (labkit 6/6 tracks persistent)
observations.E: totals.txt and rerun__starve/sheet.png: feed cut at t=300 shrinks every body (amphiphile 1984 fed vs 323 starved at t=600); the K strip ends as a single micelle

seeds_run.result: partial: no K-carrying vesicle; one K-carrying open strip; starvation dependence replicates

controls_run.E: rerun__starve/ (feed cut at t=300, seed 5) against rerun_/ (fed)

not_checked: B (no membrane-like u or K layer on this seed: u rim/core 0.83, K 0.54)
verdicts.limitation: On my seed the claimed individual, a closed vesicle with a catalyst layer on its bilayer, does not form; the catalyst persists only on an open strip, as on the author's seed 1, so 2 of 4 seeds lack it. E holds largely by construction (amphiphile is made only by K from P and decays). Very few individuals per run (one K-bearing body here). No division.
